title: Normalized finite restriction squares for the integral coefficient presentation
statement: Let l be prime, E/Q_l finite and X any scheme. Use the integral Encoding of [def-pe-integral-presentation-encoding] and normalized finite continuous-to-constant encodings of [def-pe-finite-discrete-presentation-encoding]. At each index n the exponent is n+1, and internal quotient and scalar restriction functors are those of [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] and [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. There exist an integral encoding A, encodings e_n for every positive finite quotient, and natural isomorphisms comap(q_n) followed by A.modules.functor ≅ e_n.ordinary.functor followed by completed scalar restriction. On each internal finite-coefficient module their underlying abelian sheaf maps are the identity section-action maps, expressed by the recorded equalities A.functor_eq and e_n.ordinary_functor. This is an ordinary coefficient result, with no derived comparison, transition equation, completeness, boundedness, constructibility or Noetherian hypothesis. The prime, coefficient extension and small site use [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; module sheaves and their derived categories use [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: Identify the absolute-value and spectral presentations of the continuous integer ring by an explicit identity-on-functions ring isomorphism, using equality of their topologies. The integral-limit theorem then gives the projection-normalized monoidal isomorphism to the inverse limit of constant positive quotient rings. Reconstruct commutative section rings with the same underlying additive maps.

For a finite discrete ring, send a continuous function to its finite representable section and take its adjoint under the point adjunction. Normalization on constant sections identifies this map with the inverse finite encoding. Test the integral comparison and quotient map under the point adjunction; the integral-limit projection formula says they are the same quotient function. Thus section(q_n) equals the integral comparison followed by the completion projection followed by the finite comparison.

Compose the concrete section-module equivalence with the direct restriction-of-scalars equivalence along alpha inverse. Its inverse restricts along alpha, with identity round-trip maps. The round-trip construction and triangle identity are proved for independent site-object, site-morphism, ring and module universes, then specialized here. The normalized ring square identifies the scalar actions at each finite level. Combine the existing sectionModuleComapIso with the identity scalar-action square using functor associators. Its underlying map is identity, and evaluation of the recorded functor equalities gives precisely the displayed normalization equation.

theorem integral_completion_normalized_squares :
    letI := (Padic.coefficientExtensionAbsoluteValue l E).toNormedField
    ∃ (A : Encoding l E X) (e : ∀ n : ℕ,
      FiniteDiscreteOrdinary.Encoding (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)) X)
      (a : ∀ n : ℕ,
      Mod.comap (AdicCompletion.quotient l E X n) ⋙ A.modules.functor ≅
        (e n).ordinary.functor ⋙ scalarReductionRestriction.{u, u} l E X n),
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (M : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
        (AdicCompletion.finiteRing l E X n)),
      (SheafOfModules.toSheaf (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted.{u, u} l E X)).map
          ((a n).hom.app M) =
        (SheafOfModules.toSheaf
          (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted.{u, u} l E X)).map
            (eqToIso (congrArg (fun F ↦ F.obj
              ((Mod.comap (AdicCompletion.quotient l E X n)).obj M)) A.functor_eq)).hom ≫
          (SheafOfModules.toSheaf (integralCoefficientSheaf.{u, u} l E X n)).map
            (eqToIso (congrArg (fun F ↦ F.obj M) (e n).ordinary_functor)).inv
